name: Marlowe Paige
life: “I still remember needing the price of a stamp before payroll.” People around the bank steps know Marlowe by a small Saturday habit. Marlowe takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I put down too much money to avoid looking broke. The cashier brought my change to work.
appearance: Marlowe is easy to recognize by close-cropped dark curls and a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Usually dressed in a long navy raincoat with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread, Marlowe touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word when listening.
personality: Marlowe enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To settle the deliberate overpayment in private.
family: Lennon Sanders is Marlowe’s half-sibling. Marlowe brings a spare shopping bag. Lennon chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The day sailor's divorce*, Lennon says, “I teach their son. His favorite part of Sunday is actually the walk to breakfast afterward.”
connections: Billie Wilson. A few coins needed for a bus change hands without becoming charity.
